chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

The fasting is the three days; if he fasts them, then the last of them is the Day of ʿArafah. And if he is not able to do that, then let him defer them until he fasts them among his family, and he should not fast them during travel. The correct manner of understanding this report is that it is not permissible for him to fast them during travel while believing that no option other than that is allowed for him; rather, he should believe that he is given the choice between fasting them during travel and fasting them when he returns to his family.

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةِ الْأَيَّامِ: the three days of fasting being ruled upon
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: fasting, the prescribed act under discussion
key_terms.فِي أَهْلِهِ: among his family, meaning after returning home
key_terms.فِي السَّفَرِ: during travel, the state relevant to the legal ruling
key_terms.مُخَيَّرٌ: given a choice, not restricted to only one mode of observance
key_terms.يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah, designated here as the last of the three days

ai.seo_question: Can the three compensatory fasts be observed during travel, or must they be delayed until returning home?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of fasting three days, with the final day being the Day of ʿArafah if performed in that sequence. It clarifies that a traveler is not restricted to only fasting them during travel; rather, he has the option either to fast them while traveling or to delay them until he returns to his family.
